packets.responsibility: Implements the CLAUDE.md §11 playhead pin: because #playhead is position:absolute inside the scrollable #fg-wrap, pinning ONLY the vertical axis (top=scrollTop, height=clientHeight) keeps the line spanning exactly the visible viewport at any scroll position, while `left` is deliberately left content-relative (set elsewhere, currentFrame*FC) so it still scrolls sideways with the frame it points at.
behavior: syncPlayheadToViewport (3954-3958): reads #fg-wrap and #playhead; returns undefined immediately if either is missing (no throw). Otherwise sets ph.style.top=wrap.scrollTop+'px' and ph.style.height=Math.max(0,wrap.clientHeight)+'px'.

bindPlayheadScrollSync is an immediately-invoked function (3960-3983) whose inner bind() (3961-3979): re-fetches #fg-wrap and returns if missing; attaches a 'scroll' listener calling syncPlayheadToViewport; observes #fg-wrap with a ResizeObserver when available (feedback #177: dragging #tl-resize taller, a window resize, or a panel-collapse reflow all changed the wrap's box WITHOUT firing a scroll event, so the line kept its old shorter height) and falls back to a window 'resize' listener inside a try/catch if the ResizeObserver constructor throws, or directly if ResizeObserver is undefined; then calls syncPlayheadToViewport() once immediately so the initial state is correct before any scroll/resize fires.

bind() itself runs either on 'DOMContentLoaded' (if document.readyState==='loading') or synchronously right away — the same conditional-bootstrap idiom used by the grid-resize-resync and scroll-restore-adjacent IIFEs elsewhere in this file.
callers: Invoked once by bind() at line 3980 (part of this packet).
Invoked by the DOM 'scroll' listener on #fg-wrap (line 3966) and by the ResizeObserver callback / window 'resize' fallback (lines 3975-3978) — all part of this packet's own wiring.
Invoked again at line 4215, inside the C02-owned Motion early-return branch (outside this packet, cited as a boundary), and at line 4328 inside this packet's own render-timeline Animation2D tail.
packets.effects: DOM style writes only (ph.style.top/height); listener/observer registration on module load. No state, history or render-pipeline mutation.

packets.responsibility: Re-lays out the grid (via a full renderTimeline() call) when #fg-wrap's box changes, fixing feedback #767 ('quand on resize la fenêtre du navigateur et que l'on vient d'ouvrir un projet la timeline de motion à droite ne s'adapte pas') — #frame-grid/#frame-hdr/#bars-row all get an explicit pixel width computed at render time that previously never recomputed on a bare window resize.
behavior: Module-scoped `pending` flag coalesces bursts of resize notifications into a single requestAnimationFrame callback (resync, 3986-3992): if a frame is already pending it no-ops; otherwise it schedules one rAF callback that clears `pending` and calls `renderTimeline()` only if `typeof renderTimeline==='function'`.

bindResize (3993-4000): re-fetches #fg-wrap, returns if missing; when ResizeObserver is available, tries `new ResizeObserver(resync).observe(wrap)` inside a try/catch and returns on success (silently falling through to the window-resize fallback below if the constructor throws, since the catch body is empty); otherwise (or if the try failed) attaches a window 'resize' listener calling resync.
Bootstrap: runs bindResize() on 'DOMContentLoaded' or immediately, same conditional idiom as the playhead-sync packet above.

bindResize's own bootstrap call at line 4013 is the only invocation of bindResize.
resync is invoked only by the ResizeObserver callback or the window 'resize' listener it installs.

packets.responsibility: Implements the CLAUDE.md §11 scroll-preservation invariant: every render below wipes #frame-grid/#layer-list with innerHTML='', which drops scrollTop/scrollLeft to 0; capturing before and restoring after keeps a drag/edit from snapping the timeline back to the top mid-gesture.
behavior: _tlScrollSnapshot (4015-4019): reads #fg-wrap and #layer-list by id (may be null) and returns an object carrying both DOM refs plus wrap.scrollTop/scrollLeft (0 if wrap is null) and panel.scrollTop (0 if panel is null) at call time.

_tlScrollRestore (4021-4025): returns immediately if passed a falsy snapshot; otherwise, if s.wrap exists, writes scrollTop/scrollLeft back onto it, and if s.panel exists, writes scrollTop back onto it. No return value.
callers: renderTimeline (this packet) snapshots at line 4027 (its very first statement) and restores at line 4342 (its very last statement before the closing brace) — the pattern this packet's own coverage_note attributes to CLAUDE.md §11.

packets.responsibility: Full rebuild of the right-hand timeline ruler (#frame-hdr) and grid (#frame-grid) from state, split by state.appMode into a Motion early return and an Animation2D tail; wraps the whole rebuild in the §11 scroll-snapshot/restore pair and delegates row content, playhead position, marker/BPM/audio overlays and the tween-curve/graph-editor post-passes to their existing owners.
behavior: Snapshot/ruler (4026-4051 in-scope): `_tlScrollSnapshot()` first; clears #frame-hdr and #frame-grid via innerHTML=''; computes an adaptive frame-number/second tick step (`_frameStep`/`_secStep`/`_tickStep`) from a fixed ladder [1,2,5,...,5000] so ruler labels keep >=46px apart regardless of zoom or timeline length (2026-09-03 fix for overlapping labels on long timelines), preferring an fps divisor for the frame step once frame and second labels must coexist so ticks don't fall unevenly against second boundaries.

Ruler cell loop (4052-4090ish, in-scope): for i in 0..state.totalFrames-1, creates one `.fhc` div per frame, marks the current-frame cell '.cur', and classifies each cell as a labeled second ('sec', text `Ns` using 1-based `i/fps` rounding so the boundary lands exactly at frame index `fps`, not `fps-1` — a 2026-07-25 off-by-one fix noted as previously misaligning every external frame/seconds conversion by one frame), a major frame-number tick ('tick tickMaj', 1-based i+1, only when far enough from the nearest labeled second via `_farFromSec`), or a minor tick ('tick').

Explicit width sizing (4091-4176, in-scope): computes `gridMinWidth=Math.max(state.totalFrames*FC, fgWrap.clientWidth)` and applies it to #bars-row, #frame-hdr and #frame-grid explicitly, because each is cross-axis-sized by flexbox (column-direction children) rather than by its own content — three separate 2026-07 bugs (seam between ruler and dark background, layers bleeding through the ruler area, selected-row highlight not reaching the timeline's real end) all traced to the same root cause and fixed the same way. Calls `SMTimelineZoom.redraw()` (line 4170, resyncing the custom zoom scrollbar's thumb against a totalFrames change from elsewhere, e.g. frame insert/delete or project load) and `window.updateWaBar()` (line 4171).

Mode branch (4177-4192, in-scope prologue only): `if(state.appMode==='motion')` opens a block whose SMCamera/SMMotion render calls, its own playhead left/flag writes and its own SMAudio.renderStrip() call (lines 4193-4228) plus the block's `return;` sit at lines 4193-4229, which are C02-owned and excluded (see boundaries). The branch's own explanatory comments (4177-4192) — documenting why Motion needs an early return, why it lacks a fixed rowCount formula, and three dated bugs the branch previously caused by omission (frozen playhead, missing camera row, missing audio strip) — are in-scope as comment lines even though the code they describe starts at 4193.

Animation2D branch resumes at 4230 after the omitted 4193-4229 gap and the omitted single line 4229 (SMCamera.renderGridRow(grid) for this branch, also C02-owned, the last line before this packet's second coverage_range begins): iterates `computeLayerRenderOrder()` (line 4239, folder-aware order matching renderLayerList so both panels' rows line up); for a 'folder' entry, appends a `.frow.ffolder` spacer row, optionally populating it with the representative member's own keyframe cells via `renderKeyframeCellsInto` (line 4254) when the folder is collapsed (so a collapsed Stroke/Fill/Shadow folder shows its synced keyframes instead of appearing empty); for a hidden entry, skips it entirely; otherwise appends a real `.frow` (marked '.act' if it is the active layer), sets `row.dataset.layer=li` (so DOM-index-based lookups work in both modes, a 2026-07-25 fix), calls `installLayerReorderGrip(row,li)` (line 4270) for the drag-to-reorder grip, adds extra row height from `layerCurveRowExtraHeight(li)` (line 4277) when a tween-curve strip needs it, computes `contentIdxs` (a sibling-layer index list) when the entry is a collapsed link-group head so its keyframe dots reflect ANY member's content rather than only the topmost-rendered member's (another 2026-07 fix), and calls `renderKeyframeCellsInto(row,li,contentIdxs)` (line 4300) to populate the row's per-frame cells.

Shape-tree spacer rows (4301-4314, in-scope): when `window._layerShapesExpanded[li]` is set and `SMMotion.shapeTreeRowPlan` exists, appends one `.frow.motion-group-row` header spacer plus one blank `.frow` per remaining plan entry, mirroring renderLayerList's own renderShapeTreeRowsInto row count with no content (frame data is per-layer, not per-shape).

Playhead/marker/audio tail (4315-4333, split by the omitted 4331-4332 gap): after the layer loop, sets #playhead's left via `playheadLeftPx(state.currentFrame)` (line 4327), calls `syncPlayheadToViewport()` (line 4328, this packet's own playhead-viewport-sync function) to set top/height, and sets #playhead-flag's text to the 1-based current frame. `SMMarkers.render()`/`SMBpm.render()` (lines 4331-4332) are C02-owned and excluded. `SMAudio.renderStrip()` (line 4333, in-scope again) resumes the tail, drawing the same waveform/name/mute/level rows as the Motion branch's own (excluded) call.

Post-passes and restore (4334-4343, in-scope): calls `renderTweenCurveStrips()` unconditionally (line 4334); when `SMMotionGraph.isOn()`, hides #frame-grid (`style.visibility='hidden'`) and calls `SMMotionGraph.render()` over the same box, since renderTimeline's own innerHTML wipe would otherwise silently drop the graph editor on every rebuild; finally calls `_tlScrollRestore(_scroll)` (line 4342) as the function's last statement.

This scope IS the render/DOM-sync layer: ruler tick computation, explicit grid width sizing (three related 2026-07 bugs fixed the same way), row DOM construction with folder/link-group/shape-tree awareness, playhead viewport pinning (§11), resize-triggered re-render coalesced via rAF, and post-pass integration with SMTimelineZoom/SMMotionGraph. proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: N resize notifications fired within one animation frame window.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Exactly one renderTimeline() call per rAF tick regardless of N (pending-flag coalescing), and zero calls if renderTimeline is not yet a function at fire time.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: ResizeObserver unavailable, or its constructor throws inside the try/catch.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Falls back to a window 'resize' listener; a thrown constructor is swallowed silently (empty catch body) with no re-throw and no secondary registration beyond the fallback.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: #fg-wrap/#layer-list present with nonzero scrollTop/scrollLeft/panel scrollTop; one or both absent; renderTimeline's own innerHTML wipe in between snapshot and restore.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Present elements restore their exact prior scrollTop/scrollLeft/panelTop after the wipe and rebuild; absent elements are silently skipped on both snapshot and restore with no throw.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A range of fps (e.g. 12/24/30/60) and FC (pixel-per-frame zoom) values, including ones requiring the >=46px ladder fallback beyond 5000.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Second labels land at exact multiples of fps (not fps-1); frame-number ticks appear only when far enough from the nearest labeled second; minor ticks disappear once the computed tick step reaches half a second.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: state.totalFrames*FC less than vs. greater than #fg-wrap.clientWidth.
